schema.description: What the operation is asked with.
schema.title: Asked

Medium.description:
The kinds of thing a household holds.

Named rather than passed through as the server's own word, because a surface
drawing "Series" against one server and "tvshow" against another would be
rendering a detail of which server this household runs.

`Medium` rather than `Kind`, `Holding` or `Sort`: this product already calls the two
request services a [`crate::media::Kind`], a request's suspension a
[`crate::service::asking::Holding`], and what one line of a manifest is a
`uninstall::Sort` — and one word meaning two things in one vocabulary is how a
reader comes to trust the wrong one. The contract flattens every type name into one
namespace, so a clash there is a clash for anything reading it by name.

oneOf.description: A television series, rather than one episode of one.
Something the server holds that is neither, and is not hidden for that.

Playback.description:
Somebody watching something now, as the media server lists the session.

Who and what, and where: what a household recognises about somebody watching. No
stream, no bitrate and no transcode reason, because a member is not choosing one and
a surface handed those would have to decide not to draw them.

device.description: What the device it plays on calls itself.

episode.description: The episode's number within its season, where the server numbers one.

medium.description: Which of the kinds this product deals in it is. An episode is of a series.

member.description: The name the account is known by.

member_id.description: The identifier the server files the account under.

paused.description: Whether it is paused rather than playing.

season.description: The season an episode is in, where the server numbers one.

series.description: The series an episode belongs to, where it is one.

title.description:
What is playing, in the words the server holds it under: an episode's own name
where it is an episode.
